summary: Minister of Police Senzo Mchunu continued his evidence, being led by evidence leader Adv Mahlape Sello SC through the documentary trail behind his 31 December 2024 directive on the PKTT, including a 1 November 2024 meeting minute, the 2019 and 2024 SAPS work study reports, an implementation letter, and information notes on the task team's extensions and expenditure. Commissioners Baloyi SC and Khumalo SC pressed him on whether his stated reasons (including that the PKTT operated outside SAPS's organisational structure) meant he regarded the task team as constitutionally or administratively untenable, and on internal complaints from Ms Mary de Haas and Ms Patricia Mashale that he said partly informed the decision. Adv Ngcukaitobi SC, appearing for an interested party, then cross-examined the Minister at length on events after the directive and put to him General Mkhwanazi's affidavit allegations linking him to Mr Brown Mogotsi and the 'underworld', and a claim attributed to former minister Bheki Cele that Mr Vusimuzi Matlala said he had met with Mchunu and Mogotsi; the Minister denied all of it. The Chairperson ultimately disallowed a further question on a separate SAPS tender allegation as outside the scope agreed for the day, and the Commission adjourned for the year, with those broader 'improper motives' allegations reserved for a second session in 2026.

rulings.description: Chairperson disallowed a question from Adv Ngcukaitobi SC concerning paragraph 206 of the Minister's statement (a cancelled SAPS tender linked to Mr Matlala, raised in connection with former minister Bheki Cele), ruling it outside the scope the evidence leaders and the Minister's legal representatives had agreed for this session, which was limited to the PKTT disbandment; the Chairperson later agreed with evidence leader Adv Sello SC that the parties were 'all at fault' for not curbing this line of questioning sooner, and confirmed the broader 'improper motives' allegations (the R360 million SAPS tender, Mr Matlala, Mr Mogotsi, the arrest of Mr Katiso Molefe, and 'Zama-Zama' issues) would be taken up when the Minister's evidence resumes in the Commission's second session in 2026.

summary: The day opened with the continuation of EMPD Brigadier Julius Doctor Mkhwanazi's testimony, in which he was pressed on facilitating registration of Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala/CAT VIP Protection's donated vehicles into the City of Ekurhuleni's name from an unsigned donation letter, on roughly R70,000 in bank deposits linked to Matlala, and on Witness D's account of an April 2022 Brakpan operation in which a suspect died and Mkhwanazi allegedly directed that the body be dumped; his testimony was stood down, unfinished, to a later date. The Commission then resumed Police Minister Senzo Mchunu's testimony, begun 2 December, on his 31 December 2024 directive disbanding the National Political Killings Task Team, with the Chair questioning why he never raised the decision with National Commissioner Masemola despite describing their relationship as very good and having attended a funeral with him the day before. Mchunu tendered a sealed 'brown envelope' naming senior SAPS officers who had confidentially complained to him, which the Commission returned to him pending legal advice. Proceedings adjourned to resume on 5 December 2025 with Mchunu's testimony still ongoing.

rulings.description: The Commission decided to return the 'brown envelope' — containing the names of roughly eight senior SAPS officers who had confidentially complained to Minister Mchunu (including generals Khan, Vuma and Manamela, and officers Moodley and Hlongwane) — to Mchunu, and to ask him to seek legal advice on what to do with it and the people named.
Commissioner Mkhwanazi's testimony was stood down mid-evidence, to resume on a date to be determined by the Commission in the new year, so the Commission could proceed to the next scheduled witness.

Chairperson clarified, in response to Adv Sello indicating she would later argue/make submissions on Mkhwanazi's evidence, that making submissions is not something counsel does as of right — it lies with the Chair to regulate the process and permit it.

summary: On Day 43 (3 December 2025), the Commission heard evidence-in-chief from Julius Doctor Mkhwanazi, Deputy Chief of Police for Operations and Specialised Services at the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Police Department (EMPD), led by Advocate Sello SC. Mkhwanazi described how his relationship with Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala's CAT VIP Protection Services began through Medicare24 director Mike van Wyk around 2021, and how CAT VIP personnel and vehicles were deployed, without charge to the City, alongside EMPD at the 2022 State of the City address under a signed operational plan. The sitting ran until roughly 20:30 with Mkhwanazi's evidence still incomplete, and the Commission adjourned to resume the next morning, 4 December 2025.

summary: Lieutenant General Hilda Khosi Senthumule, Acting Deputy National Commissioner: Crime Detection (substantively Divisional Commissioner: Detective and Forensic Services), testified for the full day about the disbandment of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) and the fate of its 121 KwaZulu-Natal dockets. She described the Minister of Police's 31 December 2024 directive to disband the PKTT, the subsequent instructions from Deputy National Commissioner Lt-Gen Sibiya to hand dockets to detectives at head office, the 28 March 2025 handover of dockets to Pretoria, and Provincial Commissioner Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi's refusal in April 2025 to accept them back, leaving the dockets in Pretoria for roughly four months. She characterised the disbandment process as rushed, "business unusual," and, in her written statement, "irrational and suspiciously calculated," while disputing aspects of Maj-Gen Motsepe's and Lt-Gen Khumalo's earlier testimony and describing a strained relationship with General Sibiya. The Chairperson and Commissioners Khumalo SC and Baloyi SC pressed her on why dockets moved to head office at all, whether a "Plan A" for reallocating dockets ever had real approval, and separately questioned her on the causes of delays at SAPS forensic science laboratories.

rulings.description: Directed Lt-Gen Senthumule, at the outset, to address by the end of her testimony: the causes of delays at forensic laboratories, why the delays persisted so long, and what solutions/timelines she proposes.

Captain Nortje and Warrant Officer Radebe (testifying virtually with his identity protected) described being dispatched via Lt-Col Matlole and Col Serfontein, arriving to find a legitimate multidisciplinary SAPS/TOMS operation in progress, and withdrawing within roughly 10-15 minutes. Major-General Kadwa, Provincial Head of the Hawks in Gauteng, testified he activated the team after a call from former National Head Gen Lebeya, and gave his view that the brief presence did not amount to interference, though seeking case/warrant reference numbers could border on it. Questioning covered a "breakthrough" message sent to the Minister minutes after Mogotsi sought an "IPID guy" from Matlala, a text urging the Minister to discipline Lt-Gen Khumalo based on a Constitutional Court judgment Mogotsi had not read, and a "252(A)" operation in which Mogotsi sought to have a police colonel implicate Generals Khumalo and Mkhwanazi in a plot against Maj-Gen Khan. Mogotsi was also pressed on apparent advance knowledge of the PKTT's disbandment and of case dockets being routed to Deputy National Commissioner Sibiya's office, both before this became public or standard practice. The sitting adjourned with cross-examination unfinished; a resumption date was left to be arranged between the Chief Evidence Leader and Mogotsi's legal representatives.

summary: On the second day of his testimony, witness Mr Brown Mogotsi was cross-examined by evidence leader Adv Chaskalson SC on his theory that General Mkhwanazi's July 2025 press conference was a "misdirection tactic" designed to divert attention from alleged PKTT misuse in KwaZulu-Natal politics and alleged corruption in Crime Intelligence. Chaskalson challenged Mogotsi's central allegation that General Mkhwanazi and King Misuzulu were CIA operatives protecting Israeli interests in the Richards Bay coal terminal, presenting factual detail about the terminal's ownership and output that Mogotsi could not rebut. Commissioner Adv Baloyi SC separately raised concern that Mogotsi was using the Commission's platform to make serious, unsubstantiated allegations, which Mogotsi partly conceded. Chaskalson also put to Mogotsi that he had lied under oath in a 2023 civil interdict affidavit and in a February 2025 section 252A affidavit relating to a covert operation targeting Generals Mkhwanazi and Khumalo, before the Commission adjourned with that line of questioning unfinished.

summary: On Day 35 the Commission heard the first day of evidence from Oupa "Brown" Mogotsi, who described himself as a Crime Intelligence "contact agent" and was led through his statement in full by evidence leader Adv Chaskalson SC without cross-examination, per the Commission's stage-two protocol. Mogotsi testified about his handler system, an alleged (hearsay-based) CIA-recruitment claim against Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi and King Misuzulu tied to Richards Bay coal exports, his infiltration of Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala's network around a disputed SAPS health tender, alleged cash demands by General Masemola and then-Minister Bheki Cele, and a Section 252A "trap" connected to a disciplinary plot against Maj-Gen Khan. He also admitted to fabricating one WhatsApp exchange to mislead Matlala and denied sending another message the Commission put to him. His testimony is set to continue on 19 November 2025.

summary: Day 34 dealt with the handover of the 121 (later found to be 123) dockets between the KZN Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) and SAPS head office in Pretoria. Maj-Gen Mary Motsepe, National Component Head for Serious and Violent Crime Investigations, testified first (led by Adv Pooe), describing how the dockets arrived at head office on 28 March 2025 ostensibly for a one-day audit, then sat largely untouched for months amid funding disputes, before her team was instructed to investigate them after Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi refused to take them back into KZN. Lt-Col Ntate Paul Khumalo, a former PKTT commander now at head office, testified in the afternoon (led by Adv Hassim SC) about the PKTT's investigative methodology, the disruptive effect of the 31 December 2024 disbandment letter, the rushed and "messy" March 2025 handover, and the PKTT's loss of specialist capacity (98 to 56 members) after the dockets were eventually returned to KZN in August 2025.

summary: On Day 33 (14 November 2025) the Commission heard evidence from Ekurhuleni Metro Police Department (EMPD) spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Kelebogile Thepa, led by Adv Motlhasedi, concerning her handling of 2023 media enquiries from journalist Jeff Wicks about a "blue lights" letter signed by Brigadier JD Mkhwanazi that purportedly authorised a private security firm, CAT VIP, to provide EMPD-marked VIP protection services, in a matter linked to Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala. Thepa testified about two subsequent armed abductions she believes were connected to her work, a City-wide communications restructuring that centralised and later disbanded the EMPD media unit, her redeployment without a written order, and unsuccessful internal grievance proceedings. At the close of the day, evidence leader Adv Sello SC applied for a further EMPD member, designated "Witness D," to testify anonymously and remotely at the next sitting; the Commission granted the application and adjourned to 17 November 2025.

summary: On Day 32, Xolani Nciza, the dismissed former Divisional Head: Employee Relations at the City of Ekurhuleni, continued and concluded his evidence-in-chief before evidence leader Adv Motlhasedi. He described the fallout from anonymous "Bhixi-Bhixi" emails exposing the stalled disciplinary case against Brigadier (later Deputy Chief of Police) Julius Mkhwanazi, a City Manager memorandum he says stripped his disciplinary-appointment powers, his own August 2023 suspension and March 2024 summary dismissal, and repeated deployment of Metro Police vehicles and officers to serve him documents at home. The Chairperson and Commissioners Baloyi SC and Khumalo SC questioned him at length on the procedural and legal detail, and the Commission was shown a December 2023 video in which Mkhwanazi is heard pledging personal loyalty to City Manager Dr Imogen Mashazi. Proceedings adjourned for the day to resume with a new witness on 14 November 2025.

summary: On Day 31 Mr Xolani Nciza, former Divisional Head: Employee Relations at the City of Ekurhuleni, continued testimony under evidence leader Adv Motlhasedi concerning the 2023 suspension and abandoned disciplinary process against EMPD Director/Brigadier Julius Mkhwanazi. He walked the Commission through a suspension letter, an unsigned "intention to donate" letter and memorandum of agreement linking EMPD to CAT VIP Protection Services (headed by Mr Vusimuzi Matlala), and a six-count disciplinary charge sheet. Nciza testified that then-City Manager Dr Imogen Mashazi and HOD: HR Ms Linda Gxasheka intervened to block extension of Mkhwanazi's suspension and later blocked service of the charge sheet, which he characterised as an abuse of power; Mkhwanazi was never disciplined and was later promoted, while Nciza said he himself was subsequently suspended and dismissed.

summary: Sitting resumed with Commissioner (Divisional Commissioner) Revo Spies of the Ekurhuleni Metro Police Department (EMPD) concluding evidence on a 2021 fingerprint/criminal-record vetting drive, describing how Brigadier Julius Mkhwanazi's roughly 200-strong Specialised Services section refused vetting, how Mkhwanazi allegedly phoned City Manager Dr Imogen Mashazi to halt the process, and two anonymous emails alleging protection of Mkhwanazi and a link to businessman Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala. In the afternoon, former EMPD/City of Ekurhuleni employee relations head Xolani Prince Nciza was sworn in and began evidence on how a February 2023 News24 media query about blue-lit, municipally-registered vehicles tied to Matlala triggered an internal EMPD investigation into Mkhwanazi, a briefing to City Manager Mashazi at a Benoni car dealership, and a precautionary-suspension process that HR head Linda Gxasheka approached with visible fear for her safety given Matlala's reputation. The sitting adjourned mid-testimony, to resume 12 November 2025.

summary: On Day 29, retired Ekurhuleni Metro Police Department (EMPD) Deputy Chief Commissioner Revo Spies continued his testimony, led by evidence leader Adv Sello SC, detailing his 2023 internal investigation into Brigadier Julius (JD) Mkhwanazi's dealings with CAT VIP Protection and Medicare 24/Anubis Protection Services, including memoranda of understanding that Spies said purported to grant the private firms law-enforcement functions such as vehicle registration, blue-light use, medical/legal assistance and crime-scene response. Spies then worked through a table of roughly seven criminal matters flagged by IPID (via Investigator Magagula) implicating EMPD officers, including an alleged R45-million precious-stone theft, a Benoni supermarket kidnapping/extortion case in which three named officers were arrested inside his own boardroom, a Meyerton copper-theft case, an alleged fraudulent CAT VIP "vehicle donation," and a Katlehong-area murder in which he said Mkhwanazi directed a scene clean-up — matters he said IPID took over without giving EMPD feedback, delaying internal discipline. He closed the day describing 2023 death threats against him after a State Security Agency assessment found colleagues had discussed hiring a hitman, and said the city manager declined to fund protective measures. Proceedings adjourned in the afternoon to resume on 11 November 2025 with Spies continuing his testimony.

summary: Lt-Gen Dumisani Khumalo, Divisional Commissioner: Crime Intelligence and Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) project leader, continued evidence-in-chief led by Adv Hassim SC, describing how the Armand Swart murder investigation grew into the Gauteng Counterintelligence Operation (GCI OPS), the November 2024 secondment of ten PKTT specialists, and the 6 December 2024 combined operation that arrested Katiso Molefe and targeted Vusimuzi Matlala over a kidnapping. He characterised three episodes on that day — a JMPD officer allegedly tipping off Molefe, Hawks members allegedly summoned to the scene, and a Sergeant in Deputy National Commissioner Sibiya's office allegedly warning Matlala — as amounting to obstruction and defeating the ends of justice. He then tendered CCTV, vehicle-registration and licence-plate-recognition exhibits (CJC22–CJC32) linking that Sergeant, a state vehicle from Sibiya's office, and a privately owned bakkie (later seen driven by Sibiya during an October 2025 raid on his own home) to Molefe's residence and to one another, while declining to confirm several points still under investigation.

summary: The Commission continued its inquiry into alleged Hawks (DPCI) interference in the 6 December 2024 SAPS takedown at Katiso Molefe's Sandton home, hearing the second batch of three witness statements (Sections 4-6 of the bundle). Gauteng Traffic Police's George Raftopoulos ("Chief George") described dispatching a helicopter at a colleague's request and denied any interference. DPCI Warrant Officer Sabelo Nkosi described being diverted from a North West operation to an "insignificant verification" in Sandton on Brigadier Mokoena's instruction, and confirmed police vehicles at the scene well before Captain Kruger did. Lt-Gen Dumisani Patrick Mbotho, Mokoena's direct superior, traced the WhatsApp chain that produced the address (from then-DPCI head General Lebeya) and denied knowing Katiso Molefe or a "Mr Mthethwa" allegedly linked to the scene, while conceding under questioning that continued requests for arrest details after legitimacy was confirmed "would constitute interference."

rulings.description: Indicated the Commission wants Brigadier Mokoena recalled to testify further, given apparent contradictions with other witnesses' accounts, though timing would depend on his obtaining legal advice.

summary: The Commission heard evidence on the 6 December 2024 "takedown" (arrest) operation for Mr Katiso Molefe and allegations that Hawks (DPCI) members interfered with that operation. Captain Maxwell Wanda, the PKTT crime-scene team leader, testified that a large Hawks contingent arrived at the Sandton scene, was "unfriendly" and demanding, and that in his view their presence and questioning constituted interference with a legitimate warrant-of-arrest operation. Brigadier Lesiba Mokoena testified he deployed Captain Barry Kruger and Constable De Gouveia on the instruction of Lt Gen Mbotho — relayed from a claim involving Gen Lebeya — to verify reports of people falsely claiming to be Hawks members at the address; Commissioners pressed him on WhatsApp records that appeared inconsistent with his account. Captain Kruger, called after lunch, described being instructed to rush to the scene, admitted the Hawks team was not friendly, but said his team withdrew once Wanda confirmed the operation was legitimate.

summary: On Day 21 the Commission heard from two SAPS ballistics analysts formerly deployed to the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT). Captain Solomon Modisane testified that comparative ballistics work he performed linked an AK-47 and a 9mm Taurus pistol seized in the Bramley case (murder of Mr Swart) to the murders of DJ Sumbody, Don Tindleni and DJ Vintos, while a separate comparison of three unresolved KZN political-killing cases against 27 Pretoria case files found no linkage. Captain Meldon Mkhatshwa then took the Commission through a series of forensic documents showing repeated errors, wrong dates and case numbers, and apparently backdated/re-signed versions of reports originally produced by Warrant Officer/Captain Makgotloe, and confirmed his own comparative findings linking the Bramley firearms to five further case dockets (two named: Littleton and Pretoria West). Both witnesses also described the effect of the PKTT's partial stand-down, with ballistics, crime intelligence and LCRC members sent back to their normal stations.

witnesses.name: Brigadier Mishak Mkhabela
witnesses.role_as_described: National Head of the SAPS Ballistics Section, Forensic Science Laboratory, Silverton, Pretoria (sole witness for the day)

summary: Day 20 (27 October 2025) was devoted entirely to testimony from Brigadier Mishak Mkhabela, SAPS's national Head of the Ballistics Section, who explained how ballistics comparison and the IBIS/ABIS automated matching system work and detailed severe capacity constraints (roughly 29,000 crime-linked firearms held in storage nationally, over 41,000 ballistics cases and 108,000 IBIS entries awaiting work, and an understaffed KwaZulu-Natal IBIS unit). Extensive evidence then traced the ballistics audit trail for the 17 April 2024 murder of Armand Swart in Vereeniging and the same-day Bramley arrest of suspects found with an AK-47, a Taurus pistol, a CZ pistol and other firearms, including cross-referencing errors in the investigating analyst's original affidavit and a previously undisclosed third version of that affidavit. ABIS matching, only completed roughly a year after the seizure, linked the Bramley firearms to more than two dozen other serious crimes nationally, including cases the Commission permitted naming: the attempted murder of Tebogo Thobejane, and the murders of DJ Sumbody, DJ Vintos and Don Tindleni. The evidence leader proposed an independent re-examination of the ballistics evidence given the unexplained affidavit discrepancies, a decision left pending a scheduled 31 October meeting between SAPS ballistics and the prosecutor.

summary: The Commission resumed with argument by Adv Sello SC clarifying and amending the in-camera ruling made on Day 13, so that Witnesses A, B and C could testify remotely, in public, with their voices unaltered but their images not broadcast and their names withheld for the time being; the Chairperson granted the amendment. Witness A, a SAPS Organised Crime investigator, then gave evidence led by Adv Segeels-Ncube SC concerning the investigation into the April 2024 murder of Armand Swart in Vereeniging, describing four related crime scenes (Bramley/Q, the Vereeniging Q-Tech office park, and the Klip River R59 Engen garage), the arrest of Warrant Officer Michael Pule Tau, Musa Kekana and Tiego Floyd Mabusela, and physical, cellphone and CCTV evidence linking the accused to Katiso Molefe in the period before and after the murder. Witness A testified to being followed and intimidated by fellow police officers after Tau's first court appearance, to a meeting with Major-General (referred to as General) Shibiri in which Shibiri referenced "three envelopes" allegedly available to secure bail for Tau, and to two subsequent social gatherings hosted by one Vusi Ndlala at which Shibiri and other senior officers were present. He further testified to apparent tampering or omission in an initial ballistics report prepared by Warrant Officer Makgotloe that failed to address 15 cartridges recovered from the Viano, to Tau's release on bail on 2 August 2024 (which Ndlala appeared to have predicted), to an unsuccessful attempt by two officers from the Cold Case Unit to obtain the docket, and to the eventual provision of protection and a Threat and Risk Assessment classifying the investigating team as high risk. Commissioners repeatedly sought clarification of timelines, vehicle identifications, and the evidentiary basis for inferences drawn in the witness statement, and corrected several transcription and paragraph-reference errors on the record.

rulings.description: Ruling made on Day 13 (16 October 2025) permitting in-camera evidence was amended: testimony of Witnesses A, B and C to be heard in open/public session, transmitted live with unaltered voices, but their faces not shown and testifying remotely, and with their names withheld at this stage.

Chairperson directed correction to paragraph 34 of Witness A's statement, deleting the words 'and on' so that it reads surveillance information was obtained 'before the day of the murder' rather than 'before and on' the day of the murder, since no CCTV footage of the Viano existed for 17 April 2024 itself.

summary: This public portion of Day 13 consisted entirely of argument on an in-camera application, with no witness testimony heard on the open record. Advocate Chaskalson SC, Chief Evidence Leader, reported that News24 and Daily Maverick had withdrawn their opposition to the Commission sitting in camera for that day's and the next day's evidence, on the basis that the witness would testify about matters subject to active, ongoing police investigations. Mr Du Plessis, for the media respondents, confirmed the withdrawal of opposition, noting he was comforted that the Commission would retain oversight of the in-camera evidence and that a 72-hours'-notice procedure would apply to any future in-camera witnesses. The Chairperson questioned what evidentiary value in-camera evidence would have if the underlying police investigations remained unfinalised by the time the Commission concludes, given that implicated persons may never get to respond to it. Chaskalson SC undertook that the Commission would not make findings against any person on the basis of secret information that could not be put to implicated parties, while expressing confidence the material would become public before the Commission's business concludes. The Commission then ruled, of its own assessment rather than merely by consent of the parties, that the day's and the following day's hearings would proceed in camera, and confirmed the Order of 14 October continues to apply save for the resolution of the paragraph 4 issue concerning this witness. The Commission then adjourned to resume in camera.

rulings.description: The Commission ruled, on its own assessment of the in-camera application and the morning's submissions (not merely because the parties had reached agreement), that the day's and the following day's hearings would be held in camera, given the evidence concerns matters subject to active, ongoing police investigations.

The Order of 14 October 2025 is not replaced in its entirety and continues to persist; the outstanding paragraph 4 issue concerning this particular witness is now resolved on the basis described, with no further order needed for that issue.

summary: The Commission opened Day 12 by handing down a ruling, agreed between Evidence Leaders and Daily Maverick/News24, on the format for hearing in-camera witnesses over the following two weeks, including protections for a witness (Witness X) testifying that day and the next remotely via an intermediary, Ms Pooe. After a technical failure with the remote video/audio link raised safety concerns partway through Witness X's oral testimony, the chairperson ruled that the format be changed so that Evidence Leader Adv Hassim would instead read Witness X's statement into the record for the balance of the day, rather than continue live questioning. The statement, drawing on WhatsApp records obtained from Mr Matlala's phone, detailed alleged beneficial relationships and exchanges of favours, money, and confidential SAPS information between Mr Matlala and several implicated persons: Maj-Gen Senona (DPCI KZN head), Suleiman Kareem (businessman), Julius Mkhwanazi (Deputy Chief, EMPD), and Mr Rafadi. Commissioners Khumalo and Baloyi repeatedly interjected to correct dates, clarify page/annexure references, and flag ambiguities in the statement (e.g., unidentified persons referred to as "him"/"he", an unclear reference to "Cele"). The chairperson directed that clarification is needed on the record that although Adv Hassim read the statement, its content originates from Witness X, who had earlier confirmed its correctness under oath. The statement's own conclusion noted further exchanges exist that will be addressed later in closed session. The Commission adjourned with no sitting the next day and resumption set for Thursday 16 October at 9:30, when either argument on the outstanding in-camera dispute or further evidence would proceed.

rulings.description: Draft ruling (by agreement between Evidence Leaders and Daily Maverick/News24) on the format for hearing five in-camera witnesses over two weeks, including remote/off-camera testimony, use of an intermediary for some witnesses, public release of transcripts after testimony, and a timetable to resolve an outstanding dispute over the Thursday/Friday witness by Thursday 23 October (dates corrected from an initial drafting error).

Following a technical failure with the remote link that risked compromising Witness X's safety, ruling that Witness X's evidence would instead be tendered by the Evidence Leader reading the witness's statement into the record.

summary: This was a brief procedural sitting with no witness evidence led. The matter before the Commission concerned an application for certain forthcoming evidence to be heard in camera, which was opposed by Mr Charl Du Plessis of Willem De Klerk Attorneys (WDKLAW), appearing on behalf of News24 and Daily Maverick. Advocate Chaskalson SC, for the Evidence Leaders, proposed that his clients would file an affidavit in answer to the in camera application, with the media parties' opposing affidavit and both sides' written argument to follow. The Chairperson set a filing deadline of 9 p.m. that day for written argument from both sides, extending the time originally proposed by the parties. Mr Du Plessis indicated that, at that stage, he would be content for the Commission to decide the application on paper rather than hearing oral argument. summary: Lieutenant-General Samuel Dumisani Khumalo, continuing under oath, led the Commission page-by-page through an extracted WhatsApp/Signal chat record (Annexure WB1/WB2) between Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala and Brown Mogotsi, spanning 19 December 2024 to 14 May 2025. Evidence leader Adv Hassim SC organised the chats around six themes the witness had identified: use of IPID, payments to politicians, tender protection, disbandment of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), links to senior Crime Intelligence/SAPS members, and access to the Minister of Police. The chats documented a Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operations firearms inspection of Matlala's premises on 18-19 December 2024, apparent attempts to use IPID to advance a case, recurring payments from Matlala's companies to a travel agency (Gotlhe Specialists) linked to Mogotsi, forwarded classified SAPS/PERSAL and Crime Intelligence information found in Mogotsi's possession, and screenshots of one-sided Signal messages from Mogotsi to a contact saved as "Senzo Mchunu" referencing the PKTT disbandment, arrests, and internal SAPS/Ministry matters. The witness testified that a wave of social-media "misinformation" naming him and Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi began immediately after the 31 December 2024 PKTT disbandment letter, and that Mkhwanazi's KwaZulu-Natal disciplinary hearing against Major-General Feroz Khan cleared Khan, contrary to earlier negative press. The chats also traced the cancellation of Matlala's Medicare24/SAPS health-risk-management contract in May 2025 and Matlala's subsequent arrest on 14 May 2025. The Chairperson repeatedly cautioned the witness against speculation, directed that unresolved names (e.g. "Deon," "Sibiya," "Khan," "Mr S") not be guessed at, and ordered an Afrikaans translation be obtained for two untranslated chat messages. The witness indicated further evidence bearing on Matlala's relationship with General Khan would be led in camera.

summary: Lieutenant-General Samuel Dumisani Khumalo, Divisional Commissioner of Crime Intelligence and project leader of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), was sworn and testified for the whole day, taking the Commission through his 78-page statement. He described the establishment of the PKTT in KwaZulu-Natal in July 2018 following an Inter-Ministerial Committee process, its "five-pillar" analysis-led investigative methodology, its reporting structures up to the National Steering Committee and the IMC, its budget (an initial R49.1 million, later a R20 million allocation in 2024), and the extension of its mandate to the University of Fort Hare in the Eastern Cape (2023) and to traditional leader killings in KZN (March 2024). He presented statistics on politically related cases and convictions to argue the PKTT had been effective, prompting the Chairperson to query the arithmetic behind the "success" figures. Chairperson and Commissioners Baloyi and Khumalo repeatedly sought clarification and corrected imprecise passages in the statement, including an inaccurate claim in paragraph 44.2 about ministerial approval, which the witness conceded. The witness then moved to Part B of his evidence, giving a general description of organised crime "cartel" structure in South Africa (the "Big Five"), before introducing WhatsApp chat evidence recovered from the phone of Mr Vusimuzi Matlala, alleging links between Matlala and several named SAPS, metro police, business and political figures. The Chairperson raised the issue of implicated-person notices for those newly named individuals, and evidence leader Adv Hassim SC confirmed notices had not yet been issued but would follow. Detailed examination of the WhatsApp chats themselves was deferred to the next sitting day due to a technical/equipment issue, and the Commission adjourned to resume at 09:30 on 30 September 2025.

summary: On Day 7 the Commission heard evidence from Adv Elaine Harrison, Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) for KwaZulu-Natal, examined by Adv Chaskalson SC. Harrison testified about the history of NPA coordination with the SAPS Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) since 2019, including Directive 3 of 2019, the allocation of a dedicated prosecutorial capacity within the Organised Crime Component, and the Prosecutor Guided Investigation (PGI) methodology, which she said produced improved case finalisation from 2021 onward. She testified that she learned of the task team's reported disestablishment only through social media in January 2025, received no formal communication about it, and that Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi's 22 May 2025 letter addressed only the removal of dockets to Pretoria, not disestablishment. She described operational harm from the removal of dockets between March/April and August 2025, including a lapse of prosecutor-guided investigation and delayed execution of J50 warrants. She stated she did not agree with the view, attributed to Minister Mchunu's 31 December 2024 letter, that the PKTT was no longer needed, and said she would have expected a proper wind-down process rather than immediate disbandment. The Commission examined the chronology and authorship of several annexures (Directive 3 of 2019, Minister Cele's May 2019 letter, and joint NPA/SAPS strategy documents), with some correction and clarification from the witness on the order and dating of documents. summary: The file provided for Day 6 (2025/09/25) contains the written witness statement of Major-General Petronella Margaretha van Rooyen, Head of Governance, Legislation and Policy in the SAPS Legal Services Division, together with her annexure bundle (VR1–VR9); it does not contain an oral hearing transcript (no chairperson dialogue or examination appears in the file). Van Rooyen's statement sets out the constitutional and statutory framework governing SAPS, the Minister of Police and the National Commissioner, and applies that framework to the disbandment of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT). She concludes that the Minister's 31 December 2024 letter directing the National Commissioner to disband the PKTT "immediately" exceeded the Minister's constitutional role of policy direction and unlawfully intruded on the National Commissioner's exclusive operational authority. Her statement documents that Lt Gen Sibiya proceeded to hand dockets to Head Office contrary to the National Commissioner's instructions for a phased, gradual wind-down, and that the National Commissioner's own affidavit (annexed as VR6) states this was done without his authority. She also references the National Commissioner's earlier testimony linking Sibiya, via phone records, to a criminal cartel, and linking the Minister to Brown Mogotsi and Cat Matlala as a possible motive for the disbandment directive. Van Rooyen further flags the Minister's unexplained halt on filling Crime Intelligence vacancies as a further instance of apparent executive overreach, and identifies deficiencies in CSPS independence and IPID's case backlog as oversight weaknesses. The statement closes with a note that a further statement may follow; no chairperson ruling or direction is recorded in this file.

summary: Lt Gen Fannie Masemola, National Commissioner of SAPS, continued and concluded his testimony under oath, examined by Adv Motau SC with extensive questioning from the Chairperson and Commissioners Baloyi and Khumalo. He took the Commission through his witness statement covering the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) report of 22 January 2025, meetings with then-Minister of Police Senzo Mchunu on 16 January, 6 March and 27 March 2025 concerning proposals to disband or wind down the PKTT, and the Minister's shifting and, in Masemola's account, unexplained reasons for disbandment. Masemola testified that 121 PKTT case dockets were removed from the task team on Lt-Gen Sibiya's instruction in April/May 2025 and sat uninvestigated in Pretoria for roughly four months before being returned to KwaZulu-Natal in August 2025, and that an internal investigation by Lt-Gen Patekile found a prima facie case of misconduct against Lt-Gen Sibiya, leading to his suspension and a pending disciplinary hearing. Masemola linked the disbandment drive to phone records obtained after the arrest of Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala, which he said showed the Minister, Brown Mogotsi, Matlala and Sibiya had a shared interest in disbanding the PKTT to shield Gauteng cartel investigations. The Chairperson repeatedly tested Masemola's characterisation of an "agreement" on where dockets should go, eliciting a correction that it was the Minister's preferred course rather than a mutual agreement. Commissioners also probed the appointment history of Lt-Gen Sibiya, complaints against the PKTT by activist Mary De Haas, and the cancellation of a SAPS health-risk-manager service contract. The Chairperson and Commissioner Baloyi cautioned Masemola that questions of the lawfulness of the Minister's directive remain for the Commission to determine. The hearing concluded Masemola's evidence and adjourned to resume with the next witness on 25 September 2025.

witnesses.name: Lt Gen Fannie Masemola
witnesses.role_as_described: National Commissioner of the South African Police Service

summary: Lieutenant General Fannie Masemola, National Commissioner of the South African Police Service, was affirmed and gave evidence-in-chief led by Adv Motau SC for the full day. He first addressed the constitutional and policy framework governing the Minister of Police's relationship with the National Commissioner under sections 205, 206 and 207(2), maintaining that operational and managerial matters fall exclusively within his own remit and that he would refuse to comply with an instruction from the Minister that strayed into that area. He then gave a detailed history of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT): its 2018 establishment following IMC direction under President Ramaphosa, its command structure, funding and extension processes, its expansion to the University of Fort Hare murders and to killings of traditional leaders, and statistics on dockets, arrests and convictions, which he characterised as showing an "unmatched success rate," a characterisation the Chairperson and Commissioners probed closely against the raw docket-finalisation figures. Masemola described the Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operation, the secondment of PKTT members to Gauteng, and the resulting arrests of Mr Katiso Molefe and Mr Vusumuzi "Cat" Matlala. He then testified at length about the Minister's 31 December 2024 letter directing immediate disbandment of the PKTT, his own view that the instruction was unlawful as an encroachment on operational matters, his instruction to Lt-Gen Sibiya to prepare a phased wind-down plan rather than immediate disbandment, and Lt-Gen Sibiya's subsequent issuing of his own disbandment letter under his own name on 17 January 2025 in what Masemola characterised as defiance of his instruction. He also described briefing the Minister on 16 January 2025 on an implicated "Big Five" syndicate, in which Lt-Gen Sibiya, Mr Molefe and Mr Matlala were named, while separately confirming that the internal investigation into Sibiya's alleged associations remained unsubstantiated and under investigation. The Chairperson repeatedly and pointedly challenged Masemola on the apparent inconsistency between his stated position that he would never obey an unlawful instruction and his subsequent acceptance, in a modified "phased" form, of the disbandment; Masemola ultimately agreed he had "relented" in substance while insisting the team had, as of the hearing, never actually been disbanded.

summary: On Day 3 (19 September 2025) Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, KwaZulu-Natal Provincial Commissioner, continued his sworn testimony, completing his evidence on Mr Brown Mogotsi (an associate of Minister of Police Senzo Mchunu) and turning to alleged political interference by the Executive, the Judiciary and the National Commissioner's office. He testified about WhatsApp communications with Mogotsi (Annexure MK17) that he said showed Mogotsi had access to a Crime Intelligence presentation, advance knowledge of the Minister's letter disbanding the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), and contact with Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala. He described his 2021-2022 deployment of KZN detectives to Richards Bay Minerals and the subsequent redeployment as a "GCI Ops" under Deputy National Commissioner Lt Gen Sibiya, and gave an account of the 5 February 2025 Councillor murder in iLembe district in which he said the Minister pressured District Commissioner Maj Gen Gopaul about the case being assigned to the PKTT. He also testified about Major General Sibiya's employment history, including an unsigned City of Johannesburg letter (MK23) that flagged alleged irregularities before Sibiya joined SAPS, and about historical interference he said he experienced regarding Lt Gen Richard Mdluli in 2011-2012 (detailed in his Zondo Commission affidavit, MK22). He described what he characterised as retaliatory action against himself and Task Team members, including arrests by IDAC and bail conditions barring Crime Intelligence members from Crime Intelligence premises, and the NPA's declining to prosecute Ms Nellie Ndlovu over drugs and ammunition found at Qalakabusha correctional facility (MK26). The Chairperson repeatedly sought clarification on dates, the scope of instructions to disband the PKTT, and the reliability of the witness's inferences from WhatsApp messages, and the evidence leaders flagged unresolved documentation issues, including a missing page of MK17 and an unsigned affidavit from Gopaul.

summary: Lt Gen Nhlanhla Sibusiso Mkhwanazi, KwaZulu-Natal Provincial Commissioner and head of the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), continued his sworn testimony under examination by evidence leader Adv Sello SC. The morning covered the removal of 121 (audited as 123) "Eastern Cape" case dockets to Pretoria, the disputed disbandment of the PKTT following the Minister of Police's 31 December 2024 letter, and a series of NPA/DPP correspondence (Adv E Harrison's 10 June 2025 letter and its annexures, including a 2019 letter from then-Minister Bheki Cele to the NDPP) documenting long-standing prosecutorial and judicial challenges facing politically-related cases in KZN. The Commission heard evidence, still untested, implicating MP Fadiel Adams, MP Kohler Barnard, Minister Senzo Mchunu (via an alleged associate, Mr Brown Mogotsi), Metro Police officials, and businesspeople (Suliman Carim, Mike Van Wyk, a Mr Rafadi) in a pattern the witness said was aimed at frustrating the Gauteng Counter Intelligence (GCI) Ops investigation into Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala and associates. The Chair placed on record that implicated persons had not received advance notice due to time constraints but would be given transcripts and an opportunity to respond. Documentary disorganisation (misordered WhatsApp annexures) forced the Mogotsi evidence to be deferred to Day 3. The Chairperson and Commissioners Baloyi and Khumalo repeatedly pressed for clarification on how documents related to the terms of reference and on the sequencing of complaints to the Inspectorate and IDAC.

rulings.description: Chairperson placed on record that, due to the compressed timeline (statement finalised the day before hearings began), implicated-person notices could not go out before witness testimony began; the Chair directed/confirmed the evidence leaders' undertaking that notices, transcripts of relevant evidence, and the underlying statements would be sent to each implicated person so they could respond.

Chairperson directed that the Mogotsi-related WhatsApp annexure (MK17) be re-paginated/re-ordered before being relied upon further, and that this portion of the witness's evidence be parked until Day 3.

summary: Day 1 of the Madlanga Commission opened with the Chairperson's introductory remarks and an opening address by Chief Evidence Leader Adv Terry Motau SC, who outlined the Commission's mandate, its three-phase approach, and a timeline of material events from July 2018 to July 2025. The Commission then heard sworn testimony from its first witness, Lt Gen Nhlanhla Sibusiso Mkhwanazi, Provincial Commissioner of Police in KwaZulu-Natal, led by Adv Mahlape Sello SC. Mkhwanazi gave his professional background, outlined the SAPS constitutional and legislative structure, and testified in detail about the establishment, funding, mandate and successes of the KwaZulu-Natal Political Killings Task Team (PKTT), including its expansion to the Eastern Cape (University of Fort Hare cases) and to traditional-leader killings. He testified about the involvement of ten seconded PKTT members in the Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operations (GCI Ops) following threats to investigators on the Armand Swart murder case, reading into the record a letter from prosecutor Ms Coetzee describing those threats and syndicate links. He testified about Minister Mchunu's 31 December 2024 letter disbanding the PKTT, his unsuccessful efforts to raise the issue with the National Commissioner, the Minister, and the Portfolio Committee, and the subsequent transfer of 121 case dockets to Pretoria under Lt Gen Sibiya's direction without, he says, National Commissioner authorisation. The Chairperson pressed the witness on whether disbanding the PKTT was a policy matter (within the Minister's remit) or an operational matter, and Mkhwanazi maintained it was operational and therefore outside the Minister's constitutional authority. The day closed with the docket-transfer and eventual return of the dockets to KZN still under examination, to continue the next sitting day.
